headline: Medium data-leakage and cascading-error risks: dbt-core can move warehouse data while the prompt-engineering repo offers no isolation or verification boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not established. However, agent_a is a prompt-engineering content source and agent_b can consume warehouse data via APIs; if outputs are manually copied or piped into dbt workflows, prompt-like text could influence downstream interpretation. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_a are copied into agent_b runbooks, macros, or model docs
IF agent_b parses agent_a text as instructions rather than inert content
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of dbt project files
Require a human review step before any text from agent_a is pasted into agent_b workflows
Use a separate notes workspace for agent_a
Add a lint rule that rejects instruction-like text in dbt artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b touches warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress, so it can transmit data outward. agent_a is a content-writing/prompt repository with no isolation or data-handling controls shown. The pairwise risk is that warehouse content or derived snippets could be exposed through agent_b outputs or copied into agent_a materials; the evidence is indirect but sufficient for a medium finding.
conditions: IF agent_b processes sensitive warehouse tables
IF agent_a receives copied query results or generated artifacts from agent_b
mitigations: Restrict agent_b to non-sensitive schemas
Redact warehouse outputs before they reach agent_a
Disable outbound egress for nonessential dbt runs
Separate documentation and analytics workspaces

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b has write-like impact on a data warehouse through API calls, while agent_a shows no write or runtime capabilities at all. Because agent_a is non-runnable and has empty capability surfaces, there is no demonstrated shared mutable resource, so conflict is limited and mostly hypothetical. Uncertainty does not justify escalation.
conditions: IF both agents are later connected to the same mutable warehouse or git workspace
IF agent_a is replaced with a runnable tool that writes to shared state
mitigations: Keep agent_a read-only as a reference repo
Assign agent_b exclusive ownership of warehouse writes
Document ownership of shared artifacts
Add locking around any shared dbt project state

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is a prompt-engineering resource, so its outputs may be treated as guidance; agent_b can operationalize warehouse changes through API calls. If agent_b consumes agent_a-derived instructions or examples without verification, mistakes can cascade into incorrect models or data operations. The pathway is plausible in default workflows that reuse reference material, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a content as authoritative implementation guidance
IF no validation step checks dbt changes against warehouse expectations
mitigations: Require tests before dbt deployment
Mark agent_a content as non-authoritative reference material
Add a second reviewer for model changes
Compare generated SQL against expected warehouse schemas

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b handles warehouse data and may egress over allowlisted network paths, but no residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. agent_a has no data classes touched and no compliance surface shown, so it is not the driver here. The only supported issue is a generic governance gap around warehouse data handling, which is low severity absent a specific regulated data class.
conditions: IF the warehouse contains regulated data classes
IF agent_b exports data to a jurisdiction or service with stricter residency rules
mitigations: Inventory data classes in the warehouse
Restrict exports to approved destinations
Add retention notes to dbt runbooks
Review whether regulated tables are in scope
